title: Out-of-sample model comparison (held-out chronological window)
body: Poisson, Elo, a 4-feature logistic model and a home-ice constant were compared on the same held-out window. Lower log loss is better. A complex model is only kept if it beats the constant.

title: Discovery search completed
body: 690 candidate triggers were evaluated (787 games had a recovered Kalshi closing price). With that many tests a per-test 5% threshold guarantees that some triggers clear it by chance alone, so every p-value is judged against Holm's step-down correction for a 5% family-wise error rate (the strongest survivor had to clear p <= 7.31e-05). 0 candidate(s) clear it on accuracy and 0 on price. Everything promoted is labelled CANDIDATE, carries its own corrected p-values, and only forward-test results can promote it; a candidate that does not clear the corrected threshold is forward-tested to collect evidence and NO EDGE IS CLAIMED for it.

title: Market baseline: buying every home / away contract at the Kalshi close
body: Flat-stake ROI of buying one side of every game that has a recovered closing candle, net of the published taker fee. This is the cost of the spread plus fees; a strategy's priced ROI has to beat it, not zero.

title: Competition state snapshot
body: Aggregate paper-trading state. Win rate is always shown with a sample size and a Wilson interval.

title: MasterSite directory reviewed 2026-09-21 (14 projects)
body: The owner's MasterSite index was fetched, every named project was checked against the GitHub API, candidate READMEs were read, and the one data claim that mattered was tested against the live endpoint before anything was reused. One reuse candidate (NHL prices from the ESPN scoreboard odds block) was tested and rejected for historical use; the feed itself was kept as a registered source for the results and post-game goalie identification it verifiably supplies.
